title: Seal A Driveway
dek: In the week of the 11 Sep build (v915), DAU fell 44.7% and mean concurrents 50.8% on matched weekdays, slower than the 68.6% and 67.9% of the week before. Per-player engagement fell with them on Seal alone — session length −7.6% on all five day pairs — and was back at the week-earlier level on 16 and 17 Sep.
summary: `DailyActiveUsers` 84,631 → 46,815 a day (−44.7%) and `UniqueUsersWithImpressions` 1,475,788 → 898,967 (−39.1%), Sat 09-12 → Wed 09-16 against the same weekdays a week earlier; the week before, the same comparison read −68.6% and −51.2%. Reach is 84% of the log-change in DAU and DAU per impression 16%.

Mean `ConcurrentPlayers` 1,188 → 584 (−50.8%) across the five days. The week-on-week gap narrowed day by day, from −61.0% on Sat 09-12 to −24.1% on Wed 09-16, then −6.0% on Fri 09-18 and −3.4% for 00:00–08:59 UTC today against the same hours last Saturday.

`AverageSessionLengthMinutes` 15.47 → 14.29 (−7.6%) and `AveragePlayTimeMinutesPerDAU` 20.08 → 18.01 (−10.3%), lower on 5 of 5 day pairs (paired t −3.5 and −3.7). Seal is the only one of the five games whose session length fell this week. On Wed 09-16 and Thu 09-17 both were within 1% of the week before.

`ForwardD1Retention` 10.12% → 9.26% (−8.5%), lower on 3 of 5 pairs (paired t −1.6). By source: HomeRecommendation −5.3%, Friends −5.6%, Search −10.1%, Others −14.0%; only Others is lower on all five pairs.
New players were 56.8% → 57.2% of DAU. Session length fell for new (−6.3%) and returning players (−7.6%), and re-weighting the after-window to the before-window mix changes it by −0.1%.
`DailyRevenue` R$225,645 → R$114,304 a day (−49.3%): DAU is 87% of the log-change, `PayingUsersCVR` 1.79% → 1.62% (−9.4%, 4 of 5 pairs) 15%, and ARPPU rose 3.7% to R$149.8.

Funnels read at matched cohort age: onboarding `Complete` 73.85% → 72.50% (−1.36 pp); `Progression` `TenJobs` 21.83% → 19.93% (−1.90 pp), with each later step's step-to-step rate within 2.0 pp; `MapReach 2` Airport 0.28% → 0.23% of starters.

`PlayerFeedbackVotesCount` went from 30–112 a day (04 → 10 Sep) to 205 on 09-11 and 357–408 on 09-12/13. Errors per DAU 36.8 → 38.2 (+4.0%), crash rate −1.6%, and signatures first seen at v915 or later are 0.11% of the listed 7-day error volume.

sections.timeline:
**v915** went live on **Fri 11 Sep 11:10 UTC** with the spec block *Update 10.09*: bug fixes for FPS, the airport driveway and mobile UI; a rewrite of ‘a core part of the AI code’; an invite-friend bonus (+15% cash on work earnings while an invited friend plays); a like-and-group reward (50k cash + 1 instant refill); and four sealer colours, two of them for Robux (29R and 49R). Roblox's `NEW UPDATE` event ran 09-10 18:00 → 09-13 16:55, opening about 17 hours before the build. All five portfolio games published on 11 Sep.

v916 (09-11 18:31) and v917 (09-15 12:50) were saved but not published. **v918** went live on Thu 17 Sep 15:56 and **v919** on Fri 18 Sep 15:41. **No spec was filed for either.** What the data shows about them: a new `NEW UPDATE` event from 09-17 19:00; the experience title reading `[NEW MAP🛢️]` instead of `[RELEASE 🛢️]` in the 09-19 grab (the previous grab was 09-14 16:48); error text first seen at v918 that names a `RobotHelper` DataStore and a ‘Helper price’ lookup; and step 5 of the `MapReach 2` funnel labelled NewZone rather than ParkingGarage in the latest pull.

Old servers kept running after each publish: v914 still threw errors until 09-14 (about 8.5% of all errors 09-11 → 09-14), and v918 was still throwing in the latest half-hour bucket (09-19 09:00), 17 hours after v919 went live. No thumbnail or icon change is annotated after 09-08 19:43, so none falls inside the after-window.
sections.reach:
Reach fell again, more slowly. Impressions (`UniqueUsersWithImpressions`) were −39.1% on matched weekdays against −51.2% the week before, and DAU per impression −9.2% against −35.7%. Over the five days reach is 84% of the log-change in DAU and conversion 16% (the week before: 62% and 38%). By pair, reach is the whole of the Saturday fall (impressions −56.4%, DAU per impression +0.2%) and about two-thirds of Tuesday's and Wednesday's.

By source, HomeRecommendation impressions fell 42.2% and its DAU 47.4%; Search impressions fell only 16.1% while Search DAU fell 37.1%; Friends impressions −51.5% and Friends DAU −49.9%. `Others` impressions stepped down between 09-10 and 09-11 on all five games (−31.9% to −71.9%) — the day all five published — while `Others` DAU did not step. DAU fell in each of the top 15 countries, from −11.0% (RU) to −52.6% (CA).

Home-ranking signals moved much less than reach. Of 17 RFY signals, 10 are within ±5% or moved favourably; `RFYPlayThroughRate` rose 21.1% as impressions shrank. The seven that moved unfavourably by more than 5% are the two co-play signals (D1 −9.7%, D2–7 −15.5%), the four spend signals (−8.6% to −15.7%) and not-interested users per million impressions (+7.9%). `RFYD8To28PlayDays` is served only from 09-12 and reads 0.284 → 0.212 by 09-17. Seal's DAU averaged 8.8% of its 28 Aug peak this week and was 5.6% on 09-17; Brainrot, the portfolio's measured floor, averaged 12.4% of its own peak and grew 37.3%.
sections.ccu:
Mean concurrents (`ConcurrentPlayers`, hourly) averaged 584 across Sat 09-12 → Wed 09-16 against 1,188 a week earlier (−50.8%); the week before had fallen 67.9%. The week-on-week gap narrowed through the window — −61.0% Sat, −48.4% Sun, −61.1% Mon, −37.0% Tue, −24.1% Wed — then read −32.8% on Thu 09-17 (the v918 day) and −6.0% on Fri 09-18 (the v919 day).

Today, 00:00–08:59 UTC, averages 573 against 593 at the same hours last Saturday (−3.4%) and 1,586 the Saturday before. All three Saturdays fall inside a `NEW UPDATE` event window; no ADMIN ABUSE event is annotated on this game. Hours from 09:00 had not closed at the pull and are not compared.

In the three hours after v915 went live, CCU climbed 69.3% over the four hours before, against a 42.1% climb at the same clock hours on 17 ordinary days (sd 7.7 pp, z +3.5). The v918 and v919 publish hours were within the ordinary range (z +0.75 and −0.64). Daily `PeakConcurrentPlayers` fell 53.0%, and peak concurrents per DAU fell 14.7%.
sections.retention:
`ForwardD1Retention` averaged 9.26% against 10.12% (−8.5%), after −3.5% the week before. The move is uneven across days: Sun 09-13 read 8.08% against 10.71%, while the Monday and Wednesday pairs were higher than a week earlier. Three of five pairs are lower and the paired t is −1.6, short of what five pairs need. The newest settled day, 09-16, read 10.37% against 10.11%.

By source (effect size first): Others −14.0%, Search −10.1%, Friends −5.6%, HomeRecommendation −5.3%. Only Others is lower on all five pairs (paired t −4.5). Against the binomial floor, HomeRecommendation (z −4.1), Search (−3.3) and Others (−6.4) clear it and Friends (−1.7) does not. By platform: Computer −11.1%, Tablet −10.4%, Phone −6.7%. D1 by `IsNewUser` failed inside Roblox's Explore engine and is unavailable; `ForwardD7Retention` has no settled day in the after-window (newest 09-10).

The new-player share of DAU moved 56.8% → 57.2%. Against a straight line through 08-29 → 09-10, the after-window D1 sits 4.4% below the line (z −1.2), returning-player session length 1.4% below a line that was already falling 0.15 min a day, and new-player session length 5.6% below its flat line (z −3.4).
sections.engagement:
`AverageSessionLengthMinutes` 15.47 → 14.29 (−7.6%) and `AveragePlayTimeMinutesPerDAU` 20.08 → 18.01 (−10.3%), both lower on all five pairs (paired t −3.5 and −3.7); the week before they had moved +0.7% and +0.4%. Day by day, session length first read low on the publish day, 09-11 (14.04 min against 15.12 on Fri 09-04 and 15.03 on 09-10), stayed below its week-earlier pair through 09-15, and read 15.14 and 14.94 on 09-16 and 09-17 — within 1% of 09-09 and 09-10. Session length fell on every platform: Computer −5.0%, Phone −7.2%, Tablet −8.7%.

By player type, returning-player session length had been sliding since 08-29 (18.6 → 17.4 by 09-07), read 17.44 → 17.04 → 16.67 → 15.98 across 09-08 → 09-11, and has held at 15.6–16.4 since. New-player session length read 11.89–13.11 on 09-11 → 09-15, against 12.99–14.49 on the same weekdays a week earlier, and 14.19 and 13.69 on 09-16/17.

First-play signals moved little: `RFYDuration0To60` +2.7% (higher on 3 of 5 pairs), `RFYDuration61To180` −3.1%, `RFYD1Playtime` −4.2%. The session survival curve for 09-16 → 09-19 (13.3% of sessions under 1 minute, 38.1% under 3 minutes) matches 09-05 → 09-07 (13.0%, 37.7%). Co-play fell: `RFYD1CoplayDays` 0.093 → 0.084, and down every day from 0.096 on 09-13 to 0.069 on 09-17; Friends went from 10.7% to 9.8% of DAU.
sections.money:
Revenue (`DailyRevenue`) R$225,645 → R$114,304 a day (−49.3%, after −60.7%). In the three-term split, DAU is 87% of the log-change, paying-user conversion 15%, and ARPPU −5% (it rose 3.7%, to R$149.8). `PayingUsers` 1,563 → 770 (−50.8%) against DAU −44.7%, so `PayingUsersCVR` 1.79% → 1.62% (−9.4%, lower on 4 of 5 pairs, t −2.6), after +26.2% the week before. ARPDAU (`AverageRevenuePerUser`) R$2.582 → R$2.425 (−6.1%).

At matched size the comparison depends on the weekday: at about 45K DAU, Wed 09-09 and Thu 09-10 had 687 and 636 payers against 622 on Tue 09-15; at 58–60K, Tue 09-08's 924 payers compare with 1,072 and 1,023 on the event weekend of 09-12/13. GamePass is 65.3% of revenue (67.0% before) and DevProduct 34.5% (32.9%); no item-level series exists for the four new sealer colours. First-day spend for RFY-organic players fell: `RFYD1SpendDay` −14.3% (5 of 5 pairs) and `RFYD1RobuxSpend` −15.7%. On 09-16 and 09-17, `PayingUsersCVR` read +2.5% and +27.0% against the week before.
sections.funnels:
The standard step tables above use each cohort's first read, and those reads were taken at different ages: before-window cohorts at 0.5–2.5 days old, after-window cohorts at 2.4–5.4 days old, and the 09-12 cohort in a 09-14 16:48 capture that is internally impossible — 51 of 158 cohort points in it read more than 0.5 pp above their own later value (09-11 `TenJobs` 96.8% there, 19.0% when read again on 09-19). The matched-age table below leaves that capture out and interpolates each before-window cohort to the age at which its same-weekday after-window cohort was read.

At matched age, onboarding (`FUNNEL_TYPE_ONBOARDING`) is close to flat: `ReachedDriveway` −0.14 pp, `PouredOut` −0.51 pp, `DrivewaySealed` −1.40 pp, `Complete` 73.85% → 72.50% (−1.36 pp, lower on 4 of 5 pairs). `Progression` loses players at `TenJobs`: 21.83% → 19.93% (−1.90 pp, −8.7%), with its step-to-step rate from `FirstUpgrade` 24.8% → 22.7%; the step-to-step rates after it held (`FirstRebirth` 81.0% → 80.3%, `SecondArea` 95.2% → 95.3%, `FirstTruck` 63.7% → 61.7%). `MapReach 2`: `EstateDistrict` 13.04% → 11.72%, `RetailPark` 1.55% → 1.33%, `Airport` 0.28% → 0.23%.

The spec's airport-driveway item is measurable only in counts. Of players whose map funnel started 09-03 → 09-15, 2,009 reached the Airport and 184 of them (9.2%) reached step 5; for 09-16 → 09-19 starters, 108 and 15 (13.9%), z +1.4. Windows spanning August read 11.5–14.0% on the same ratio. Step 5 is labelled NewZone only in the latest pull, so the 09-16 → 09-19 figure straddles v918.
sections.technical:
The standard technical table pairs Tue 09-15 with Tue 09-08, the day Roblox telemetry collapsed FPS and memory on all five games at once (F28); that one pair accounts for its +11.7% FPS p10 and +37.0% memory %. With it removed (and the Seal-only 52.3 ms reading on 09-13 removed from client CPU time): client FPS p10 46.80 → 43.69 (−6.7%), average FPS 61.67 → 53.46 (−13.3%), client memory % 20.72% → 23.82% (+15.0%) while client memory in bytes fell 13.5%, crash rate 0.50% → 0.47% (−5.5%), OOM exits per DAU −9.0%. Server frame rate p10 is flat at 59.95.

Those moves sit on a level shift on **09-09, two days before v915**, with no Seal build published between 09-04 and 09-11: average FPS 63.9 (05–07 Sep) → 53.6 (09–10 Sep) → 53.8 (12–18 Sep), memory % 19.9% → 24.4% → 23.6%. The other four games moved −1.0% to −6.5% on FPS over the same days, against Seal's −16.1%. Within Seal, Computer moved most (FPS p10 46.7 → 38.6, memory % 15.4% → 25.7%), then Phone (FPS p10 46.9 → 43.6), and Tablet least (50.9 → 49.3). Over 12–18 Sep Computer FPS p10 read 41.1 and Phone 44.3; neither is back at its 05–07 level.
sections.errors:
`ErrorCount` per DAU was 36.8 → 38.2 (+4.0%). Client errors are the bulk of the volume (09-12: 1,673,208 client against 20,138 server). Server errors per DAU read 0.26–0.35 on every day 09-12 → 09-17 and 0.83 on the v915 publish day. In the unfiltered 7-day export, one warning first seen at v488 (`ContextActionService could not find the function passed in`) is 81.3% of the listed total and an animation-track-limit warning (v639) another 17.1%.

Signatures first seen at v915 or later total 10,506 events in that export, 0.11% of the listed volume. The largest are an EditableImage-not-accessible error on the race-surface render path (8,390, client, first seen 09-14 18:22 UTC) and an engine-level mutex error with no game script in its trace (2,116, first seen 09-15 17:31, the day the Windows and Mac 739 clients were released). Below them: upgrade saves failing after three tries on DataStore 502s (306), oversized unreliable remote payloads (280, split by byte count), a `RobotHelper` DataStore save failing (89, new at v918), client script timeouts (61), MapReach funnel-mark read/save failures (33), and coverage-shortfall warnings — a finished surface not paid or recorded when the server had seen only 0.01–0.08 coverage (31, on Neighbourhood and EstateDistrict surfaces; the message embeds the value, so this is a floor). The table pairs each class with the rate that would move if it mattered.

Inside the before-window, server errors reached 72,724 and 329,833 in the 16:00 and 16:30 half-hours of Sat 09-05, and five comments about lost progress arrived between 16:34 and 16:38 that afternoon.
sections.sentiment:
Written comments have thinned out: 225 on builds up to v901, 114 on v908, 36 on v914, 14 on v915 and 2 so far on v918–919. The downvote rate read 80% (v908) → 69% (v914) → 64% (v915); both v919 comments are upvotes. On v915, AI art or a listing that does not match the game appears in 3 of 14 comments, rebirth and pacing in 3, performance in 2, the paywall in 2 and a surface that will not finish in 1. A lost save or purchase appears in 1 of 14 (an unlimited-sealer item bought before release that no longer applies), against 7 of 36 on v914 (six rows, one a duplicate, between 16:34 and 16:38 on 09-05). No v915 comment names the airport; one v914 comment on 09-09 did.

By device, performance language stays on Computer: 2 of 6 Computer comments on v915 and 0 of 8 Mobile (Phone + Tablet); 3 of 21 and 0 of 15 on v914; 9 of 42 and 6 of 72 on v908. `PlayerFeedbackVotesCount`, a separate series from written comments, went from 0.47–1.34 votes per 1k DAU on 04 → 10 Sep to 4.47 on 09-11 and 4.10–6.78 on every day since; written comments did not rise with it.
sections.method:
- **Window.** Sat 09-12 → Wed 09-16 against Sat 09-05 → Wed 09-09, paired by weekday. Both windows begin the day after a publish that came with a `NEW UPDATE` event (v914 with 09-04 18:00 → 09-07 19:00; v915 with 09-10 18:00 → 09-13 16:55). The before-window's Monday was inside its event and the after-window's Monday was not.
- **Instrument faults removed.** 09-08 is the portfolio-wide telemetry fault (F28): every FPS, memory and CPU comparison is re-run without that pair. `ErrorCount` for 09-08 is only a partial read and is missing. Client CPU time on 09-13 (52.3 ms, Seal only) is excluded; the 09-15 client-CPU dip appears on all five games.
- **Funnels at matched age.** Cohort completion keeps rising for a week or more, so steps are compared at equal cohort age using every raw capture; the 09-14 16:48 capture is excluded as non-monotone. The standard step tables above are first reads and are kept for provenance.
- **CCU.** `ConcurrentPlayers` hourly buckets that had not closed at the 09:12 UTC pull are dropped; today is compared on hours 00–08 only.
- **Feedback.** The corpus `feedback.csv` is truncated by today's short grab; all comment counts use the merged file (391 rows). Build = the version the player was on when writing.
- **Error exports** are capped at their top rows; counts on messages that embed a surface, a value or a byte count are floors, and absence is not evidence.
- `PlayerFeedbackVotesCount` is labelled net (up − down) in this pipeline and no up/down split is served.
- `TotalSessionsEndedInBucket` is read as a survival curve — inferred from its shape, not documented.
- The trend lines in the retention section are descriptive extrapolations over 13 post-peak days; they are not forecasts.
sections.diagnosis: Two different things moved on Seal this week and they need separate explanations. The volume fall — DAU, concurrents, revenue — is mostly reach, and it slowed sharply by 18–19 Sep. The per-player fall — session length, playtime, payer conversion, and more weakly D1 — is specific to Seal among the five games, is not a change in who arrived, begins on the v915 publish day, and had closed by 16–17 Sep without another build. The hypotheses below take each candidate in turn, most explanatory first; the ones marked ruled out or weakened are results, not omissions.

hypotheses.title: Reach kept falling on a post-peak curve, and the fall is slowing
hypotheses.claim: Most of this week's volume loss is the continued withdrawal of distribution after the 28 Aug peak, now decelerating; it does not need v915 to explain it.
for: Reach is 84% of the log-change in DAU (impressions −39.1%, DAU per impression −9.2%); on the Saturday pair it is 100%.
Every volume series slowed: DAU −68.6% → −44.7%, impressions −51.2% → −39.1%, mean CCU −67.9% → −50.8%; CCU week-on-week read −6.0% on 09-18 and −3.4% for 00–08 UTC today.
Ranking signals moved far less than reach: 10 of 17 RFY signals are within ±5% or favourable, and `RFYPlayThroughRate` rose 21.1% as impressions shrank.
The fall is broad: every acquisition source lost DAU (−35.5% to −49.9%) and every one of the top 15 countries did (−11.0% to −52.6%).
Seal is 19 days past its peak at 8.8% of it this week; the two other games still falling (Banana Monkey −58.7%, Verity −40.2%) are also on post-peak curves.
against: It does not explain the per-player rates: session length −7.6% and playtime −10.3% on 5 of 5 pairs, which reach alone cannot move.

Seven signals did fall by more than 5% (co-play days, the four spend signals, not-interested per million impressions), so the clean ‘every signal flat’ signature of an external reach cut does not hold.
Competitive displacement and Roblox-side ranking changes cannot be tested from one universe; they stay unresolved inside this hypothesis.
hypotheses.test: Week-on-week DAU and CCU for Sat 09-19 → Wed 09-23 (DAU served ~09-25). A fall within about ±15% would say the curve has flattened near 5–6% of peak, the depth at which Brainrot stopped falling.
hypotheses.lever: Reach levers — content cadence, creative, re-engagement notifications — sized against a game now at 5–6% of its peak, not a code fix.

hypotheses.title: A Seal-only engagement dip in the five days after v915 went live, session length back by 16 Sep
hypotheses.claim: Something specific to Seal shortened sessions and lowered payer conversion from 11 to 15 Sep; the v915 publish is the timing candidate, but the dip reversed without another publish and no mechanism is identified.
for: Session length −7.6% and playtime per DAU −10.3% on 5 of 5 pairs (paired t −3.5 and −3.7), after +0.7% and +0.4% the week before.
The day-by-day drop begins on 09-11, the publish day (14.04 min against 15.12 a week earlier), and every day through 09-15 is below its pair.
Seal is the only one of the five games whose session length fell (the others +0.4% to +13.7%), and it ranks last of five on playtime per DAU, D1 and first-play bounce.
Not composition: new-player share 56.8% → 57.2%; re-weighting to last week's mix changes session length by −0.1%; new (−6.3%) and returning (−7.6%) sessions both fell, on every platform.
Matched-age funnels lose players at `TenJobs` (step-to-step 24.8% → 22.7%), the first step that takes sustained play rather than the tutorial, while onboarding holds within 1.4 pp.
`PayingUsersCVR` −9.4% (t −2.6) and `RFYD1SpendDay` −14.3% (5 of 5 pairs) move with it.

The dip is Seal's alone: session length against the other four games 0.93 on 11 Sep, 0.86–0.93 on 12–15 Sep, back to 0.97 on 16 Sep (*against the other four games, day by day from 08 Sep* (At a glance)).
against: It closed without a build: session length −0.2% and −0.6% on 09-16/17, playtime −0.1% and +0.5%, D1 +2.6% on 09-16; nothing was published between 09-11 and 09-17 (v917 was saved, not published).

Returning players' session length had been sliding since 08-29 (18.6 → 17.4 by 09-07) and its steepest drop runs 09-08 → 09-11, partly before the publish; in the after-window it sits only 1.4% below its pre-publish line.
D1 is weak support: 3 of 5 pairs lower, paired t −1.6, with the Monday and Wednesday pairs up.
No logged defect fits: v915+ signatures are 0.11% of error volume, and the largest (8,390) first appears on 09-14, three days into the dip, and does not stop when the dip does.
The v915 publish drew a stronger-than-usual CCU climb (+69.3% against +42.1%, z +3.5), so the build did not visibly repel players on the day.

It did not fully close against the portfolio: D1 index 0.81–0.89 on 11–16 Sep, impression→play CVR 0.72 and 0.66 on 16–17 Sep, and `RFYD2To7PlayDays` 0.84 and 0.81 on 16–17 Sep stay below the other games after session length recovers (*against the other four games, day by day from 08 Sep* (At a glance)).
hypotheses.test: Session length and D1 for 09-19 → 09-23 (served ~09-21 → 09-25) against both earlier weeks: holding at the 09-16/17 level (about 15 min) would confirm the dip was transient. A matched-age `TenJobs` step-to-step for cohorts 09-16 → 09-19 back near 24.8% (readable ~09-23). A hands-on session on v919 through the first ten jobs would show whether anything in that stretch still slows play.
hypotheses.lever: First-session pacing on the core loop up to ten jobs, measured by `TenJobs` step-to-step and session length.

hypotheses.title: A Seal-only client performance shift on 09-09 costs players, Computer most
hypotheses.claim: Client FPS fell and memory % rose on Seal alone on 09-09, with no Seal publish, and the spec's FPS item in v915 did not bring the level back; part of the returning-player slide may belong to this shift rather than to v915.
for: Average FPS 63.9 → 53.6 and memory % 19.9% → 24.4% between 05–07 and 09–10 Sep; the other four games moved −1.0% to −6.5% on FPS against Seal's −16.1%.

Computer moved most (FPS p10 46.7 → 38.6, memory % 15.4% → 25.7%) — the device class that carries the lag reviews (2 of 6 Computer comments on v915, 9 of 42 on v908, against 0 of 8 and 6 of 72 on Mobile).
Returning-player playtime per DAU fell 24.48 → 23.39 → 22.32 across 09-08 → 09-10, before v915.
The level did not return after v915: average FPS 53.8 over 12–18 Sep, Computer FPS p10 41.1 against 46.7.
against: D1 (10.11%, 9.93%) and all-player session length (15.17, 15.03) on 09-09 and 09-10 were at their usual levels.

It lands the day after the portfolio-wide telemetry fault and alongside the engine 738 releases, and client memory in bytes fell 15.6% while memory % rose — an odd pair for a real regression — so a change in how the metric reads for this game cannot be excluded.
Crash rate by platform over 12–18 Sep is back near its 05–07 level; per-player performance averages lose the players a regression drives away, so they cannot size its cost.
hypotheses.test: A profile of v919 on a mid-range Windows client against the ~64 FPS average of 05–07 Sep, and `ClientFpsAvg` by platform for 09-19 onward (served ~09-20).
hypotheses.lever: A client render and memory budget on Computer, measured by Computer `ClientFpsP10` and Computer D1.

hypotheses.title: The like-and-group reward shipped and is being used
hypotheses.claim: The v915 reward for liking the game shows up as a step in feedback votes on the publish day.
for: `PlayerFeedbackVotesCount` per 1k DAU read 0.47–1.34 on 04 → 10 Sep, 4.47 on 09-11 and 4.10–6.78 on every day since; raw votes 205 on 09-11 and 357–408 on 09-12/13.
The step lands on the publish day and has held for a week.
against: The series is labelled net (up − down) and no split is served, so ‘more upvotes’ cannot be told from ‘fewer downvotes’.
Written comments did not rise (1–3 a day), and votes are not a Home-ranking signal, so no reach effect is expected or visible.
hypotheses.test: The dashboard's up/down vote split for 04 → 18 Sep; any vote or rating trend read across 11 Sep is not like-for-like.

hypotheses.title: v918/v919 (the ‘NEW MAP’ builds) steadied concurrents
hypotheses.claim: The two builds at the right edge, with a new event and a title that now advertises a new map, may be why the week-on-week CCU fall shrank to −6.0% on 18 Sep and −3.4% this morning.
for: The title reads `[NEW MAP🛢️]` in the 09-19 grab, a new `NEW UPDATE` event started 09-17 19:00, and the funnel's step 5 is now labelled NewZone.
against: The deceleration was already under way with no publish (−37.0% on Tue 09-15, −24.1% on Wed 09-16).
Neither publish hour departed from ordinary days (z +0.75 and −0.64), and 09-17 was the lowest mean-CCU day of the window (403).
The week-earlier Friday and Saturday were also inside an event; no spec exists for either build; v918 was live alone for under 24 hours, so the two cannot be separated on daily metrics.
hypotheses.test: DAU, Home and Search impressions and D1 for 09-18/19 (served 09-20/21), then the matched week 09-19 → 09-23 (~09-25). A Search-impression rise after the title change would be the most direct sign.
hypotheses.lever: If it holds: content cadence as a reach lever, measured by impressions and CCU week-on-week.

hypotheses.title: The airport-driveway item in v915 unblocked late progression
hypotheses.claim: If the server-side coverage blocker at the airport was fixed, more players who reach the Airport should go on to the next map step.
for: Airport → step 5 read 13.9% (15 of 108) for funnel starts 09-16 → 09-19 against 9.2% (184 of 2,009) for 09-03 → 09-15 (z +1.4).
No v915 comment names the airport (0 of 14); v908 and v914 each had one.
against: The numbers are tiny and the difference is not significant; the 09-16 → 09-19 window straddles v918, which relabelled step 5 NewZone, so it is not a clean read of v915.
Coverage-shortfall warnings are still logged at v915, at 0.01–0.08 coverage on Neighbourhood and EstateDistrict surfaces.
At matched age the share of starters reaching the Airport went 0.28% → 0.23%, and August windows already read 11.5–14.0% on Airport → step 5, before any fix.
hypotheses.test: Airport → step 5 for cohorts 09-19 → 09-25 read at 7+ days (from ~09-26), against the August 11.5–14.0%; an error export filtered to v919 searched for Airport coverage rows.
hypotheses.lever: If the blocker persists: the server's coverage threshold on airport surfaces, measured by Airport → step 5.

hypotheses.title: The new Robux sealer colours lifted spend
hypotheses.claim: The two paid colours (29R, 49R) added to what payers spend.
for: ARPPU +3.7% (R$144.4 → R$149.8); DevProduct share of revenue 32.9% → 34.5%.
against: ARPPU was higher on only 3 of 5 pairs (t +1.0); payer conversion fell 9.4% and first-day spend 14.3–15.7% over the same days.
No item-level revenue series exists, so the colours cannot be isolated from the rest of the shop.
hypotheses.test: A dashboard monetization export by product for the two colour products since 09-11.

hypotheses.title: The invite-friend bonus raised Friends traffic and co-play
hypotheses.claim: A +15% cash bonus while an invited friend plays should raise Friends arrivals and the share of days played with a friend.
for: Nothing measurable in aggregate. The bonus pays only when an invited friend joins and invites are not instrumented, so an effect on a small group would not show in these series.
against: Friends DAU −49.9% against total −44.7%, Friends share of DAU 10.7% → 9.8%, and Friends new users lower on every weekday pair.
`RFYD1CoplayDays` −9.7%, falling every day from 0.096 on 09-13 to 0.069 on 09-17; `RFYD2To7CoplayDays` −15.5%.
D1 for Friends arrivals −5.6%, in line with the other sources.
hypotheses.test: An in-game event for invite sent and invited friend joined, or a count of bonus-bar displays; a hands-on check that the bar appears when a friend joins.

hypotheses.title: Errors introduced by v915, v918 or v919 are costing players
hypotheses.claim: A defect logged in the new builds explains the week's rate moves.
for: New classes did appear: an EditableImage-not-accessible error on the race-surface render path (8,390), upgrade-save failures after three DataStore retries (306), a new `RobotHelper` DataStore failure at v918 (89).
against: Signatures first seen at v915 or later are 0.11% of the listed 7-day volume; errors per DAU +4.0%; server errors per DAU unchanged (0.26–0.35); crash rate −1.6% (−5.5% with the fault day removed).
The largest new signature first appears on 09-14, three days after the engagement dip began, and continues after it ended.
No v915 comment reports a lost save; one reports a purchase from before release that no longer applies (1 of 14 match the lost-save-or-purchase pattern).
hypotheses.test: A since-v919 7-day export on 09-25, checking whether any top row points at a surface whose rate is moving; silent defects stay possible and are tested through the funnels, not the export.

hypotheses.title: The before-window was distorted by the 09-05 save incident
hypotheses.claim: The Sat 09-05 server-error burst and lost-progress reports make the before-window an unfair baseline.
for: Server errors reached 72,724 and 329,833 in the 16:00 and 16:30 half-hours of 09-05, against 941–1,755 per half-hour in the two hours before, and five lost-progress comments arrived 16:34 → 16:38.
against: That day's D1 (11.13%) and session length (15.03) sit within the before-window's range, and the Saturday pair's session drop is the same size as the others'.
Any damage would lower the before-window and shrink this week's measured falls; it cannot create them.
hypotheses.test: Already settled by the per-pair table; no further read needed.

hypotheses.title: A change in who arrived (new vs returning, source, country) explains the rate drops
hypotheses.claim: The per-player rates fell because the mix of players changed, not because the game held them less.
for: Source shares did shift: HomeRecommendation 64.0% → 61.0% of DAU, Others 18.2% → 21.3%.
against: New-player share 56.8% → 57.2%; re-weighting to last week's mix changes session length by −0.1% and playtime by −0.2%.
Session length fell for new and returning players and on every platform; D1 is lower on Home, Search and Others, the three sources with enough volume to read.
DAU fell in all 15 top countries (−11.0% to −52.6%), so no single region carries the move.
hypotheses.test: Settled by the mix and source tables.

hypotheses.title: A platform-wide or seasonal shock this week
hypotheses.claim: Roblox-wide demand or an instrument change moved every game the same way this week.
for: Three platform-wide items exist and were set aside: the 09-08 telemetry fault (FPS/memory on all five), the 09-15 client-CPU dip (all five), and the 09-11 `Others`-impression step (all five — though all five also published that day).
against: Two of the five games grew this week (Brainrot DAU +37.3%, Waterslide +71.1%) while three shrank.
Seal is the only game whose session length fell, and D1 fell only on Seal and Verity.
hypotheses.test: Settled by the five-game table; re-run on the next matched week.

hypotheses.title: A thumbnail or listing change moved this week's numbers
hypotheses.claim: A creative swap inside the window cut conversion or retention.
for: Players still name the AI art: 3 of 14 v915 comments, 5 of 36 on v914 — a brand item, separate from this week's movement, and the reach version of this theory was already tested and killed on 09-10.
against: No thumbnail or icon change is annotated after 09-08 19:43, so none falls inside the after-window; the title change to `[NEW MAP🛢️]` comes after it.
`RFYPlayThroughRate` rose 21.1%, and the per-player falls include players who never see a listing (returning players' session length −7.6%).
hypotheses.test: None needed for this window; the D1-by-source method stays the test for any future creative question.

reads.what: Client FPS, memory and crash rate for 09-19, the first full day with v919 live (still mixed with v918 servers).
DAU, revenue, session length and RFY signals for 09-19, the first behavioural day after v919 — whether session length held at the 09-16/17 level (H2) and whether DAU kept the slower slope (H1).
D1 for the 09-19 cohort; Home and Search impressions for 09-18/19 against the title change (H5).
Full matched week Sat 09-19 → Wed 09-23 against 09-12 → 09-16: DAU, CCU, D1 by source, session length, `PayingUsersCVR`; since-v919 7-day error export.
Funnel cohorts 09-19 → 09-23 at 3+ days' age: `TenJobs` step-to-step against 24.8% (H2) and Airport → step 5 (NewZone) against August's 11.5–14.0% (H6).
